clue.text: Diana served one master

indicators.note: served in the sense of dished up in a new way, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A goddess, or a woman called Diana, worked faithfully for a single employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' reads as the verb of a servant, but it signals the anagram of I and MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman huntress goddess Diana is identified with her Greek counterpart Artemis.

clue.text: It's a crime to knock the Vicar's block off

indicators.note: to knock a head off is to remove the first letter
block is slang for head, so the word loses its top letter

parts.note: a vicar is a parson; the possessive gives no letters

explanation.surface: Beheading a clergyman is criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'block' is slang for head, so knocking it off removes the P of PARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a crime.

clue.text: Composition of animal in new coat

indicators.note: the animal is placed in the other letters
new means the coat is remade in a different arrangement

parts.note: a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A pet wearing a new coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' looks like a school essay; it is a keyboard piece. 'new' rearranges the coat, and 'in' puts the animal within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a musical composition for keyboard, showing off the player's touch.

clue.text: African gazelle with additional sound

indicators.note: sound says the word is said out loud rather than spelt

parts.note: additional means more

explanation.surface: A gazelle with an extra noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The mohr is a North African gazelle.

clue.text: Dumb waiter that can be fired?

definitions.text: Dumb waiter that can be fired?

parts.words: Dumb waiter that can be fired?
parts.note: a dumb waiter can be a revolving server at table; one that can be fired is a soldier's pistol

explanation.surface: A rotating tray for serving food that can be shot like a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: A dumb waiter is a lazy Susan, a server that revolves; 'fired' turns it into a handgun issued to officers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the standard-issue revolver of the armed forces, punned as a revolving server.

clue.text: 18 of boy found in vehicle

indicators.note: the boy is found sitting inside the vehicle, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Dave is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A grisly discovery: something belonging to a lad turns up in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 points to the answer at 18-across, a dead body, which this answer also means.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a dead body, the same thing as the corpse at 18-across.

clue.text: Government's grudging support for research?

parts.note: research into science, conscience read as con-science, and money given reluctantly as if from guilt

explanation.surface: Ministers reluctantly hand over funds for scientific study.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the money as funds for science; in fact it is anonymous payment made to soothe a guilty mind, such as unpaid tax sent to the Treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to relieve guilt, often to the Treasury, which wryly matches a grudging grant.

clue.text: Academic given crucial post finds it mere drudgery

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
key means crucial
a post is a job, or work

explanation.surface: A lecturer who lands an important job finds it tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey work is the dull, laborious part of a task.

clue.text: Wise old queen kept a device for fine adjustment

indicators.note: the queen keeps the other piece inside her

parts.note: VR, Victoria Regina, is Queen Victoria
Ernie Wise was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A sagacious elderly monarch held on to a precision instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise old' reads as one description; Wise is the comedian Ernie Wise, and VR is the old Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: A vernier is a sliding auxiliary scale for making fine measurements and adjustments.

clue.text: Chants from scripture lessons led to rebellions

indicators.note: led to says one piece goes in front of the other

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, was the old name for scripture lessons in British schools
chants means sings

explanation.surface: Hymns sung in RE class sparked uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, is the old British school name for scripture lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Risings are uprisings, revolts against authority.

clue.text: With tea-bag first put in sweetener

indicators.note: first says the bag comes before the tea, though the clue writes tea-bag the other way round

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch
char is British slang for tea
something put in is in

explanation.surface: Instructions for a brew: drop the tea-bag in first, then add sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea-bag first' looks like a brewing tip; 'first' really orders the pieces, bag before tea, against the clue's word order.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial sugar substitute used to sweeten drinks.

clue.text: Spies hunted fabulous creature first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved round to the end of the word

parts.note: Lewis Carroll's poem The Hunting of the Snark is about pursuing that imaginary beast

explanation.surface: Secret agents went after a mythical beast from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' sounds like a whole hunt from start to finish; it moves the S of SNARK to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nark is British slang for a police informer, someone who spies for the authorities.

clue.text: Bread for which leper loses heart

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letters of the word are taken away

parts.note: Naaman was the Syrian commander cured of leprosy by Elisha in 2 Kings 5

explanation.surface: A sufferer from leprosy grows dispirited over the bread on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The leper is a specific Bible figure, Naaman; his central MA goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a leavened flatbread from Indian cookery.

clue.text: New directions require prudence

indicators.note: new directions suggests these letters are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: Fresh instructions call for a careful approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective on directions; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Discretion is careful judgement, a synonym of prudence.

clue.text: Any East London assembly is unique

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Any gathering in the East End is one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' looks like a meeting, but it rearranges ANY, E and LONDON.
explanation.definitionFit: The one and only means the single unique example of something.

clue.text: Where Rome couldn't win, Scots can't

definitions.meaning: the battlefield in Apulia where Hannibal crushed the Roman army in 216 BC
in Scots dialect the word for cannot is spelt with a closing -nae

explanation.definitionFit: Cannae is both Hannibal's great victory over Rome and the Scottish form of cannot.

clue.text: Straight from the factory — Dagenham, say?

definitions.meaning: goods priced as sold directly at the factory gate, before delivery
Dagenham in east London was once Ford's huge car plant, so it is a former works

explanation.walkthrough: Dagenham was Ford's British car factory until vehicle assembly ended there in 2002, making it a works of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex-works describes goods sold at the factory, and read as ex works it means a former factory.

clue.text: Chemical affecting the incidence of lice?

parts.note: a nit is the egg or young of a louse
incidence means the rate at which something occurs

explanation.surface: Some substance changes how often people catch head lice.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'the incidence of lice' as a rate of nits: NIT RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a salt of nitric acid, a common chemical compound.

clue.text: Writer and publisher of Titbits?

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
Geoffrey Bles was a London publisher, known for the first Narnia books

explanation.surface: Who wrote and published the magazine Titbits?
explanation.walkthrough: Tit-Bits was a British magazine; here titbits are morsels.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibbles are small snacks, titbits.

clue.text: Model and beat musician — seller of skunk, perhaps

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
a rapper performs words over a beat

explanation.surface: A fashion model and a rap star are dealing cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: Skunk suggests strong cannabis; here it is the animal, whose fur a trapper sells.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapper catches animals such as skunks and sells their pelts.

clue.text: 5 found right in the wood

indicators.note: the right is found inside the wood, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

explanation.surface: Five people discovered in the trees on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 points to 5-across, a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse is a dead body, the same as the cadaver at 5-across.

clue.text: Instrument used only under fire

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places this piece below the other

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
but means only

explanation.surface: A gun used only when shot at.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is a Renaissance forerunner of the trombone.

clue.text: Where decisions are made about poor road-sweepers

indicators.note: the sweepers go round the other letters, one piece wrapped about another

parts.note: brooms are sweepers

indicators.note: poor suggests the road is in bad shape, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Councils decide in committee about badly kept roads and street cleaners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' jumbles the road's letters, and 'about' wraps the sweepers round them, splitting the sweepers after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Boardrooms are where company directors meet to take decisions.

clue.text: Polecat, get away!

parts.note: S is short for south, one of the earth's poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shoos a smelly polecat away.
explanation.walkthrough: The word Polecat is split into Pole (S) and cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is an exclamation used to drive an animal or person off.

clue.text: Subject beloved of the egotist?

parts.note: taken as written
the egotist's favourite word is me

explanation.surface: The topic the self-centred person loves best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beloved of' links the egotist to the first-person pronoun, the self-centred person's favourite subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Race abandoned in Algeria?

annotationWithheld.why: Race abandoned in Algeria? (4) for ORAN: no parse found giving O + RAN or otherwise; 'abandoned' has no clear letter source

clue.text: Plant almost like a wolf

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of the end

parts.note: lupine is the adjective meaning wolf-like

explanation.surface: A flower that is nearly wolfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant's name does come from the Latin for wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like flowers.

clue.text: Senior cleric, unfortunately never competent

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: competent means able

explanation.surface: A complaint that a high-ranking churchman is sadly never up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns NEVER into VENER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable is the title of an archdeacon in the Church of England, so it stands for a senior cleric.

clue.text: Direction to collect aerosol

parts.note: S, for south, is a compass direction
a collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy

explanation.surface: An instruction to gather up a spray can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collect' is not the verb but the noun, a short church prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a can that sprays its contents, so a kind of sprayer.

clue.text: Any detritus gets thrown into the river

indicators.note: detritus is debris broken into pieces, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: thrown suggests letters tossed about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Any rubbish ends up tipped into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detritus' turns ANY into YAN and 'thrown' turns GETS into GTSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtse is China's longest river.
